question: What is the difference between default, parameterized, and copy constructors?

scenes.sub: Three ways to bring an object to life.
scenes.say: Default, parameterized, and copy constructors. They differ only in what you hand the new object. One small Point class shows all three.

scenes.head: One class, three constructors
scenes.say: The default constructor takes no arguments. Point a gets zero, zero. The parameterized constructor takes the values you choose, so b is three, four. The copy constructor builds a new Point from an existing one. It takes a const reference to another Point, and copies each member. Both spellings, equals b and parentheses b, call it.

scenes.head: Trap: copy constructor or copy assignment?

panels.code:
void show(Point p);   // takes a Point by value

Point c = b;          // copy constructor
show(b);              // copy constructor (into p)
c = a;                // copy ASSIGNMENT

scenes.say: When is the copy constructor called? Initializing a new object from another one. Passing by value, which copies into the parameter. And returning by value, unless the copy is elided. But c equals a is not a constructor call at all. c already exists, so this is copy assignment, operator equals. Interviewers love that one: the equals sign alone doesn't tell you, whether a new object is being created does.

scenes.head: Two more traps
scenes.say: Two more traps. First: once you write any constructor yourself, the compiler stops generating the default one, so Point p no longer compiles. Add Point equals default, or write one, to get it back. Second: the copy constructor must take its argument by reference. Taking it by value would need a copy, which calls the copy constructor, forever. So the language forbids it.

scenes.head: Side by side
rows: Only if you declare no constructors
Yes, unless you declare a move
scenes.say: Default takes nothing, parameterized takes your values, copy takes a const reference to the same type. Examples on screen. And generation: you get a default constructor only if you declare no constructors at all. A copy constructor is generated automatically, unless you declare a move operation, which deletes it.

lines: Default: no arguments. Lost as soon as you declare any constructor.
Parameterized: builds the object from values you pass.
Copy: from another object of the same type, taken by const reference.
scenes.say: Default: no arguments, and lost as soon as you declare any other constructor. Parameterized: built from the values you pass. Copy: a new object from an existing one, taken by const reference. And remember, assigning to an existing object is copy assignment, not the copy constructor.
